messages.body_plain:
Hi everybody,
I'm starting to use JGR and I find it really good.

But I noticed that concerning the graphics:

- the figure margins are not the same as running the scripts directly in

than doing it from the original R graph Window (save as metafile), which 
are really good.

Am I having a wrong installation or the JGR features for graphs do have 
JavaGD this limitations?

Thanks!

boris.

> I'm starting to use JGR and I find it really good.

> Am I having a wrong installation or the JGR features for graphs do

> JavaGD this limitations?

Neither. The PDF is not produced by JGR, it is produced by R's "pdf 
()" device. Unfortunately JGR has nothing to do with this. Can you be  
more specific as of how you exactly use the output?
Copy/paste will not work for publications as that produces a bitmap.  
MS software cannot handle PDF properly (despite the fact that PDF is  
of much higher quality than metafile), but then hopefully you're not  
using that software for publications ;). In the unlikely case you do  
(and are really using Windows), you pretty much have to use the  
metafile export (of course you can do that from JGR - see ? 
win.metafile).

Cheers,
Simon

On Oct 15, 2007, at 10:11 AM, Erich Neuwirth wrote:

> I dar to crosspost, since I already asked on r-help and did not get an

That's fine - anything JGR/iplots related should go here.


> iplots:
>
> Is there a way to set position and size of the windows from the  
> code? I want to set up a multiwindow set of linked graphs for a  
> demo, and i would like them to pop up in place without the need of  
> resizing and moving around.
>

Yes, but only the location (see iplot.location). I shall add  
iplot.size for the next release (or possibly make it an option in  
iplot.opt instead).

For now, you can use the following "hack":

iresize<-function(w, h, plot=iplot.cur()) {
     if (is.numeric(plot))
         plot <- .iplots[[plot]]
     if (inherits(plot, "iplot")) {
      .jcall(plot$obj,,"setSize", as.integer(w), as.integer(h))
      .jcall(.jcall(plot$obj,"Ljava/awt/Frame;","getFrame"),,"pack")
     } else stop("invalid plot")
}

iplot(rnorm(100))
iplot.location(250,250)
iresize(200,200)


Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Testing recent JGR; some little questions
messages.subject_clean: Testing recent JGR; some little questions
messages.body_plain:
Just dropped in to test JGR to see how it might work with students.
Thanks for your sustained effort.

I had a few first impressions.

1.  I think this "run JGR() as root" thing is inconvenient.

> JGR()
Please consider running JGR() as root to create a start script in
/usr/lib/R/library/JGR/scripts/run automatically.
Starting JGR ...
Warning message:
In file(con, "w") :
  cannot open file '/usr/lib/R/library/JGR/scripts/run', reason
'Permission denied'
> sh: /tmp/RtmpEaMO4K/jgrs327b23c6: No such file or directory


Can't you add JGR() as a last command to run as part of the JGR
install script?  When our computer lab systems update, and a new JGR
is installed, it won't work until I go around to each one and run this
manually.


2. I have a problem saving graph output.  A new R installed recently,
perhaps that's the trouble.  In JGR, I run.

Loading required package: rJava
Loading required package: iplots
Creating per-session help links...
> x <- rnorm(100)
> hist(x)

### Then I used the pull down menu File | save eps.

> Error in .javaGD.copy.device(source, useDevice, file = file, ...) :
  could not find function "dev.cur"


If I type "?dev.cur" then I do see the help page, but the grDevices
package has not loaded. After I manually load that package

> library(grDevices)

Then the JGR file | save does create the output file.

Would you say R is wrongly installed here?

3.  I wish the File | Save As EPS feature were a bit richer.

Or you could relabel it "postscript" rather than "eps".

I believe it is not generating encapsulated post script because, as
far as I can tell, there is no bounding box.  In the graph I generated
with JGR, the first line looks like this:

%!PS-Adobe-3.0

Whereas after I generate a true EPS file, I see this:

%!PS-Adobe-3.0 EPSF-3.0^M

The difference is important in generating LaTeX output in pdf format.
There are unexpected problems concerning the horizontal/vertical
positioning of the graph.

I believe that, in R, if you specify onefile=F, then it causes the
postscript output to be turned into EPS, with a bounding box as well
as a preview image.

4. I wish your Save As option allowed me to specify "horizontal = false".

-- 
Paul E. Johnson
Professor, Political Science
1541 Lilac Lane, Room 504
University of Kansas

Paul,

On Oct 22, 2007, at 12:51 AM, Paul Johnson wrote:

> Just dropped in to test JGR to see how it might work with students.
> Thanks for your sustained effort.
>
> I had a few first impressions.
>
> 1.  I think this "run JGR() as root" thing is inconvenient.
>
>> JGR()
> Please consider running JGR() as root to create a start script in
> /usr/lib/R/library/JGR/scripts/run automatically.
> Starting JGR ...
> Warning message:
> In file(con, "w") :
>  cannot open file '/usr/lib/R/library/JGR/scripts/run', reason
> 'Permission denied'
>> sh: /tmp/RtmpEaMO4K/jgrs327b23c6: No such file or directory
>

That is actually a bug - JGR() generates a temporary shell script, but  
unfortunately it is deleted before the shell can read it. I have fixed  
that for the next release.


> Can't you add JGR() as a last command to run as part of the JGR  
> install script?

I'm not quite sure what you mean - there is no "JGR install script".


>  When our computer lab systems update, and a new JGR is installed,  
> it won't work until I go around to each one and run this manually.
>

In most cases it should be safe to use the same script, so you should  
not need to re-run it. Note that the script is meant to be linked or  
copied by the sys admin to some reachable location (e.g. /usr/bin or / 
usr/local/bin) - the JGR() command is merely a convenience function to  
make it simple for users that don't know much about Linux. It is  
easier to use the script directly to start JGR than calling JGR() in R.


> 2. I have a problem saving graph output.  A new R installed recently,
> perhaps that's the trouble.  In JGR, I run.
>
> Loading required package: rJava
> Loading required package: iplots
> Creating per-session help links...
>> x <- rnorm(100)
>> hist(x)
>
> ### Then I used the pull down menu File | save eps.
>
>> Error in .javaGD.copy.device(source, useDevice, file = file, ...) :
>  could not find function "dev.cur"
>
>
> If I type "?dev.cur" then I do see the help page, but the grDevices
> package has not loaded.

This is often caused by old preference files hanging around. Old  
versions of R didn't have grDevices, so chances are that your  
preference file is that old and you didn't enable grDevices in the  
Package Manager since. A clean JGR will add it automatically, but if  
you have a preference file, it will override it. Removing  
~/.JGRprefsrc is recommended when upgrading major JGR or R versions  
for those reasons.


> After I manually load that package
>
>> library(grDevices)
>
> Then the JGR file | save does create the output file.
>
> Would you say R is wrongly installed here?
>
> 3.  I wish the File | Save As EPS feature were a bit richer.
>
> Or you could relabel it "postscript" rather than "eps".
>
> I believe it is not generating encapsulated post script because, as
> far as I can tell, there is no bounding box.  In the graph I generated
> with JGR, the first line looks like this:
>
> %!PS-Adobe-3.0
>
> Whereas after I generate a true EPS file, I see this:
>
> %!PS-Adobe-3.0 EPSF-3.0^M
>
> The difference is important in generating LaTeX output in pdf format.
> There are unexpected problems concerning the horizontal/vertical
> positioning of the graph.
>
> I believe that, in R, if you specify onefile=F, then it causes the
> postscript output to be turned into EPS, with a bounding box as well
> as a preview image.
>

Fair enough, I'll change the export to onefile=FALSE (yes, JGR just  
calls R to produce those files).


> 4. I wish your Save As option allowed me to specify "horizontal =  
> false".
>

We don't use custom save dialog, so there is no easy way to add that.  
However, as a 'hack, you can always define your own pdf or postscript  
function and change any of the parameters, since the call is evaluated  
in the global environment. This is not nice, but gives you full  
flexibility for the time being.

Thanks for your comments!
Simon

> ("(.packages())"), Rengine.eval(".libPaths()"), they are working  
> fine. But when I tried the following functions, Rengine.eval 
> ("suppressWarnings(try(.getContent(varName),silent=TRUE))",  
> Rengine.idleEval(".getModels()"), Rengine.idleEval(".getOtherObjects 
> ()"), they are not working. Error message shows that those  
> functions are not found.
> Can somebody please help me with this question?


They are in the JGR package. You have to install and load the JGR R  
package "library(JGR)" in order to access those function and they are  
internal to JGR, so they work only in conjunction with JGR.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: trouble compiling rJava; can't compile JNI program
messages.subject_clean: trouble compiling rJava; can't compile JNI program
messages.body_plain:
On 10/23/07, Simon Urbanek <urbanek at research.att.com> wrote:
> Because you have to configure R's Java support to match your Java
> distribution. There are many different Java distributions and they
> need different paths flags etc. By default R on Debian comes without
> Java support enabled (because it is optional), so you have to add it
> to match your configuration. In theory this should be done when Java
> is installed, but then Sun doesn't know anything about R ;).
>
> Cheers,
> Simon

I totally understand & agree on the need for something like R CMD javareconf.

I recall that I did have to reconfigure/rebuild R to enable java last
year, but I think the RPM from Fedora is built with java now and I've
not had to rebuild an RPM.  It makes sense that their RPM would be
built against a different java compiler.

I'm just a little disappointed/frustrated that there's no apparent
documentation that points the average user in this direction.  I saw
the error message about java from iPlots and rJava for months and
could not figure it out.  There's no comment about javareconf as an
option when you look at the R man page or output from R --help.  If I
didn't get the bright idea of asking you directly, I never would have
figured it out.

I run a script as a cron job every night so that packages are updated
and to install packages that I want on our systems.  It will be easy
enough to run R CMD javareconf every night as a part of that script.
I'll suggest to the Fedora RPM maintainer that R CMD javareconf be
added to the post install script.  Might save some hassle for average
users.


-- 
Paul E. Johnson
Professor, Political Science
1541 Lilac Lane, Room 504
University of Kansas
